articles.excerpt: CVE-2026-12411: Cross-Guest Volume Hijack via DevLXD Device PATCH in Canonical LXD Vulnerability ID: CVE-2026-12411 CVSS Score: 8.4 Published: 2026-11-05 CVE-2026-12411 is a broken access control vuln…
articles.body: CVE-2026-12411: Cross-Guest Volume Hijack via DevLXD Device PATCH in Canonical LXD Vulnerability ID: CVE-2026-12411 CVSS Score: 8.4 Published: 2026-11-05 CVE-2026-12411 is a broken access control vulnerability in the DevLXD interface of Canonical LXD versions 6.6 through 6.8. The flaw resides in the devLXDInstancePatchHandler component, which fails to verify storage volume ownership when an instance attaches a new disk device via the /dev/lxd guest socket. When the security.devlxd.management.volumes configuration option is enabled, an untrusted guest or DevLXD identity can issue a crafted HTTP PATCH request referencing another tenant's custom storage volume.

articles.body: Originally published on Homingo Learn . Fear on a phone screen comes from where the camera stands and where the light falls. What each choice does, how to plan it shot by shot and how to build it for flat 2D art in code. Horror cinematographers work with a short list of tools: where the camera stands, how it moves, and which part of the frame the light is allowed to reach. An animated vertical Short uses the same tools, with two differences. The frame is tall and small, so every choice has to read at a glance on a phone. And there is no set: a camera move is a transform on your art layers, and a light is a layer you draw. This guide covers both halves, the film grammar and the code for it. articles.body: The shortcut to writing faster with voice input is to separate two steps: dictating a rough draft by voice, and having AI clean it up. Spoken words don't become a manuscript on their own, so the approach is two-stage: generate volume with your voice, and let generative AI shape it into prose. For freelancers who spend a large part of their week on blog posts, client reports and newsletters, the first draft is usually what eats the most time when everything is typed. Combining voice input with AI cleanup noticeably shortens the time to a finished first draft. Here is a workflow you can run day to day.

articles.title: What's inside a GPU? Cores, streaming multiprocessors and the memory problem
articles.excerpt: A modern GPU is not one very powerful processor. It is thousands of simple arithmetic cores grouped into streaming multiprocessors, plus specialised tensor cores for matrix maths and ray-tracing cores…
articles.body: A modern GPU is not one very powerful processor. It is thousands of simple arithmetic cores grouped into streaming multiprocessors , plus specialised tensor cores for matrix maths and ray-tracing cores for light simulation, all surrounded by schedulers, caches and a very wide memory system. The hard engineering problem isn't the maths. It's moving data fast enough to keep all those cores busy. What are CUDA cores? Most of the work runs on simple parallel arithmetic units. NVIDIA calls them CUDA cores , AMD calls them stream processors (inside its compute units), and Apple simply counts GPU cores . Each is much simpler than a CPU core, but there are thousands of them running the same instruction across different data at once.

articles.body: "LoRA trainiert etwa 1 % des Modells" ist die übliche Ein-Satz-Erklärung. Sie stimmt, verschweigt aber die Teile, die entscheiden, ob ein Lauf auf deinen Rechner passt und wie lange er dauert: welche Layer Adapter bekommen, was der Rank an der Anzahl ändert, in welcher Präzision die eingefrorenen Gewichte liegen und wie viele Optimizer-Schritte ein kleiner Datensatz tatsächlich ergibt. Hier sind diese Zahlen für einen konkreten Lauf durchgerechnet: Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, Rank 16, auf einem Mac mit Apple Silicon und 16 GB. Die Einstellungen sind die Standardwerte des lokalen Trainers in der Desktop-App osFoundry , einem ganz normalen Skript aus transformers + PEFT + TRL. Die Rechnung lässt sich also auf jedes ähnliche Setup übertragen.

articles.body: For a startup that mainly needs business email, Zoho Mail is far cheaper than Google Workspace . That's because Workspace charges for a whole productivity suite. If your team lives in Docs, Drive, Meet and Gemini, Workspace earns its price. If you need reliable email with proper admin controls, Zoho is the easy call. Prices are what I saw when I set this up. Both change, so check current pricing. Why does business email cost so much? articles.title: Earth has captured a new mini moon  — but it won't stick around for long
articles.excerpt: Earth has caught itself a new mini-moon, and QQ8 is sticking around for Christmas.
articles.body: Earth has caught itself a new mini-moon, and it is sticking around for Christmas. The space rock, designated 2026 QQ8, was first observed in August 2026 after entering orbit around Earth in April 2026. The discovery was reported by the International Astronomical Union's Minor Planet Center on Thursday (Oct. 29). The stay of QQ8 is a temporary one. The mini-moon will remain in the thrall of Earth's gravity through December before breaking away in 2027. Scientists have recreated the orbital path of QQ8, finding that it takes 359 days, or about 0.98 of an Earth year, to orbit the sun . QQ8 closely approaches Earth around once every ten years, but this time the object came so close that Earth has been able to gravitationally seize it.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 5, 2002: NASA's Galileo spacecraft flies by Jupiter moon Almathea only to find it's a 'pile of icy rubble less dense than water'
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 5, 2002, NASA's old Galileo spacecraft flew by a small moon called Amalthea and made a surprising find. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 5, 2002, NASA's old Galileo spacecraft was almost out of fuel. But the Jupiter mission still had some science to do. Galileo flew by a small moon called Amalthea. Amalthea is small, but it's interesting for scientists. The Jupiter moon Amalthea is the reddest object in our solar system. It also generates more heat than it gets from the sun. Scientists think Amalthea creates electrical currents as it orbits in Jupiter's huge magnetic field. Near this little moon, strong radiation from Jupiter is dangerous for spacecraft. The flyby caused some problems for Galileo. The spacecraft went into safe mode only 30 minutes after going past Amalthea. NASA said it was ready for problems, because Galileo was on its last legs, and the radiation near Amalthea was strong.
articles.author: Hanneke Weitering

articles.title: You don't have to go to the moon to see Earth differently: Artemis II astronaut Victor Glover on what really matters
articles.excerpt: After a record-breaking journey around the moon, Artemis 2 astronaut Victor Glover explains why you don't need to travel into space to see Earth differently.
articles.body: TENERIFE, Canary Islands — Imagine traveling over 250 million miles from home, watching Earth disappear behind the moon and losing contact with the billions of people who call it home. What would you miss most? For Artemis II astronaut Victor Glover, the answer wasn't a particular place, a familiar view or even the comforts of home. It was something much more fundamental: human connection. Speaking during a discussion with former astronaut Chris Hadfield at the Starmus VIII festival on Oct. 18 in Tenerife, Canary Islands, Glover reflected on the extraordinary experience of traveling around the moon and how being so far from Earth had given him a renewed appreciation for the people living on it. "The greatest reason to go to space, it isn't to be a swashbuckler hero," Glover said.

articles.title: NASA's Voyager 1 probe bounces back from communications glitch in interstellar space
articles.excerpt: NASA's Voyager 1 probe is back in communication after the 49-year-old spacecraft briefly fell silent last month, during its interstellar-space mission.
articles.body: Voyager, 1, humanity's most distant spacecraft, is back in contact after briefly losing touch with Earth last month. The spacecraft stopped phoning home for about 48 hours between Oct. 18 and 20 due to a communications glitch that Voyager 1 resolved on its own, before engineers could send the long-running spacecraft a remote fix. "This is the first time we've seen the spacecraft do something like this, but we are also at a point in the mission where we have to expect the unexpected," Kareem Badaruddin, Voyager mission manager at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL), said in an agency statement about the incident on Oct. 29.
